title: Structured Contributor Onboarding and Observable Outcomes
author: Aisha Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines a standardized, competency-centered onboarding pathway for individual contributors and IC+ roles that focuses on observable outcomes, measurable checkpoints, and a lightweight certification at the end of the probation period. It synthesizes recruiting handoffs, manager preboarding, the first 90-day plan, and the role certification rubric into one reference.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time IC hires (engineers, data scientists, product managers, design) and long-term contractors converting to headcount.
- Not a substitute for team-specific immersion rotations; it is the baseline that every manager must implement and adapt.

Principles

1. Observable outcomes over subjective impressions: define three concrete signals of success by day 30, 60, and 90.
2. Manager-led but cross-functional: managers own delivery; peers and platform teams provide access, mentoring, and code reviews.
3. Lightweight, evidence-based certification: avoid long forms — evidence is artifacts (PRs, docs, dashboard) and short rubrics.
4. Equity and consistency: every candidate receives the same minimum set of resources, timelines, and evaluation criteria.

Quick summary checklist (manager preboarding, to be completed before new hire start)

1) Offer to onboarding handoff completed by People Ops (relevant docs & benefits)
2) Manager: welcome note and 90-day objectives sent to candidate and people-ops on calendar (template below)
3) Access requests created: cloud account, code repo, Slack, ticketing, payroll
4) Hardware order placed and delivery ETA confirmed
5) Buddy assigned and 1:1 schedule for first 6 weeks created

Detailed 90-day outcome map

| Time window | Focus area | Observable signals (examples) | Owner |
|-------------|------------|-----------------------------|-------|
| Day 0–30 | Orientation & small-impact delivery | Onboarding PR merged; one customer-facing doc updated; first meaningful code review completed | Manager + Buddy |
| Day 30–60 | Ownership and integration | Independent ownership of one minor feature or bug sprint; demonstrates monitoring/alert understanding; contributes to design discussion | Manager + Tech Lead |
| Day 60–90 | Scale & impact | Delivers feature to production or ships measurable improvement; mentor a peer during handoff; documents runbook or operational checklist | Manager + Product/PM |

Procedures and templates

A) Manager welcome note (email/Slack template)

```
Subject: Welcome to Redwood — first week plan
Hi [Name], welcome to the team! For your first week please expect: 1) orientation call at 09:30 on Monday; 2) access & device setup; 3) a short pairing session with [Buddy]. My 90-day outcomes for you are attached — we will review them on day 7 and weekly after. Let me know any questions. — [Manager name]
```

B) First week schedule (minimum)

- Day 1: HR & benefits overview (People Ops), team kickoff, hardware check, security briefing
- Day 2: Dev environment setup, first story assigned (small), buddy pairing
- Day 3: Product context deep-dive, metrics & dashboards intro, local run of service
- Day 4: Cross-functional sync & design walkthroughs
- Day 5: Small demo + retro with manager and buddy

C) Evidence capture & folder structure (required)

- Personal onboarding folder: /teams/<team>/onboarding/<firstname_lastname>
- Required artifacts: onboarding PR link, first feature ticket, monitoring/dashboard screenshot, 30/60/90 retrospective note

Role certification rubric (end of probation — 90 days)

Instructions: Manager and tech lead jointly score the IC on 5 criteria; use 1–5 scale (1 = not observed / 5 = exceeds expectations). Pass threshold: average >= 3.25 and no single criterion < 2.

| Criterion | What to look for | Example evidence |
|-----------|------------------|------------------|
| Technical delivery | Completes assigned tasks; code quality; shipping to prod | PRs merged, release notes, peer review comments |
| Product/context understanding | Knows customer goals & metrics | Dashboard snapshots, design notes, tickets linked to metrics |
| Collaboration & communication | Participates in async & sync, gives/receives feedback | Meeting notes, code review feedback, stakeholder threads |
| Operational ownership | Understands alerts, oncall basics, runbooks | Runbook created/updated, incident toy example handled |
| Learning velocity & initiative | Seeks feedback, grows skills quickly | Training completions, paired sessions, mentorship notes |

Scoring matrix (example)

- 5: Consistently above expectations; independently improves processes
- 4: Meets expectations and occasionally exceeds them
- 3: Meets expectations with normal guidance
- 2: Partially meets expectations; several gaps require active coaching
- 1: Does not meet expectations; escalation required

Decision outcomes and next steps

- Pass: IC is certified into role. Update HR systems, set next-level goals, consider increased autonomy and ownership.
- Conditional pass: Extend probation 30 days with documented improvement plan and weekly check-ins.
- Fail: Initiate offboarding or role change procedure per HR policy. Always coordinate with People Ops and Legal for risk & compliance steps.

Escalation and support flow

- If scoring shows any criterion <= 2 after week 8, manager must notify People Ops and present evidence-based improvement plan within 5 business days.
- People Ops will triage, recommend coaching resources, or escalate to Director-level review if necessary.

Operational playbooks and integrations (quick links)

- Access request template: /confluence/eng-infra/access-request-playbook
- Device procurement SLA: device should be delivered by day 3 where possible, see /confluence/people-ops/hardware-and-equipment-guidelines
- Security onboarding checklist: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth

Metrics and reporting

Each manager should report aggregated onboarding health monthly to People Ops including: time-to-first-PR, time-to-production, percent passing probation, and mean rubric scores. People Ops will run quarterly analyses to detect systematic bias or bottlenecks (e.g., hardware delays, access failures).

Manager responsibilities (summary)

- Own writing and communicating the 90-day outcomes before start date.
- Schedule and run weekly 1:1s for first 12 weeks.
- Collect evidence artifacts and score with tech lead at day 90.
- Escalate concerns early and partner with People Ops.

Appendices

A. Example 90-day outcome template (editable)
- Outcome 1 (30d): [short description, acceptance criteria, artifact link]
- Outcome 2 (60d): [short description, acceptance criteria, artifact link]
- Outcome 3 (90d): [short description, acceptance criteria, artifact link]

B. Short checklist for buddies

- Intro to team norms and cadence
- Schedule three pairing sessions in weeks 1–3
- Provide at least two inline review examples and one retrospective on day 30
